newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hope of interest rate cut to lead Seoul shrs rise.
newsitem.headline: Hope of interest rate cut to lead Seoul shrs rise.

text.p: The Seoul stock market is expected to maintain its recent upbeat trend throughout Thursday, bolstered by still lingering anticipation of a cut in interest rates, brokers said.
But they forecast consolidation would limit a repeat of the hefty rises on the index seen yesterday.
The composite stock index closed on Wednesday 2.53 percent higher at 817.78.
Brokers said many investors believed a cut in interest rates was imminent, which will help ease corporate financial standing and improve market liquidity.
"Active buying by domestic institutional investors will remain strong in low-priced large-cap shares, such as Daewoo Group shares," said Woo Sang-cheol of Tongyang Securities.
Brokers said institutional investors became liquid after they unloaded their shares following the expansion of South Korea's foreign stock ownership ceiling on October 1.
"They need to change their investment portfolio after the stock sales. They are hunting for bargains," Woo said.
But individual investors, having no confidence on the market direction and the nation's economy, would show selective buying interest in small-cap shares for quick profits.
